quest.title: The Long-Failed "Graph Adversarial Technology"...
quest.description: After putting in some work, you have collected enough samples. Looks like it's time to follow up with Lepine-Pauline...
quest.rewards_formatted: "Special Analysis Zoom Lens" x1, Mora x10000, Adventurer's Experience x4

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Isn't that Charlotte?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What could she want with Lepine-Pauline...?

dialogues.speaker: Lepine-Pauline
dialogues.text: Pretty please with a cherry on top, Charlotte! Journalist extraordinaire! Please tell me you're joking!

dialogues.speaker: Lepine-Pauline
dialogues.text: I read that a gang of criminals tricked the Gardemeks by disguising themselves as Blubberbeasts... It's true, isn't it? It has to be!

dialogues.speaker: Lepine-Pauline
dialogues.text: I've invested all of my savings into Graph Adversarial Technology, and even taken out a sizeable bank loan!

dialogues.speaker: Lepine-Pauline
dialogues.text: I'm begging you! Begging you like the beggiest beggar in all of begdom!

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: Okay, okay, I need you to calm down a little, Miss Lepine-Pauline...

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: I admire your passion for your research, and I don't mean to dash your hopes for those, um... big-ticket orders...

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: But... I'm afraid I'm not joking. The Blubberbeast incident was a short story mailed to us by an anonymous amateur author, written in the style of a true story.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh... Paimon sees what happened here...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Sounds like the "report" Lepine-Pauline read in The Steambird wasn't in the news section after all...

response.speaker: Charlotte
response.text: Funnily enough, I actually remember being in a meeting where the editing team was debating the potential risk of misleading the public with this story. They even went to the Maison Gardiennage for advice.

response.speaker: Charlotte
response.text: But to our surprise, they fully supported us printing it. They figured that the false intel would be a great way to dupe potential criminals into wearing ridiculous costumes when breaking the law...

response.speaker: Charlotte
response.text: In truth, Gardemeks are extremely sophisticated in their capabilities. They can identify criminals just as reliably as the best human Gardes, so a crude disguise isn't gonna get you far. If anything, it'll just make you stand out all the more...

response.speaker: Charlotte
response.text: Since we ran that story, the Maison Gardiennage has made a slew of arrests including, uh... one "Phantom Blubberbeast," a "Titanic Redcrown Finch," and a "Specterman"...

response.speaker: Charlotte
response.text: So I knew this story had helped out law enforcement, but this is the first time I'm learning of an innocent citizen being deceived by it... And investing so much Mora for nothing...

response.speaker: Lepine-Pauline
response.text: *whimpering*... Aaaaaah...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh-oh... so Lepine-Pauline's whole research project is based on a fictional story?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Which means we're not gonna get a big bonus after all? ...But more importantly, she's gonna lose everything she's invested...

response.speaker: Charlotte
response.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon! You're back!

response.speaker: Charlotte
response.text: I was in the area taking some photos for a story, when I got talking to Miss Lepine-Pauline about her research. She told me about your collaboration.

response.speaker: Charlotte
response.text: She was hoping I could write an article to spread awareness about image recognition technology. She even paid me for the article and gave me one of her prototype devices before I could get a word in...

response.speaker: Charlotte
response.text: I unfortunately had to dash her hopes, and I'm afraid all your hard work was in vain, too. She's desperately trying to find a way to rescue the project and get you the Mora you're due... I've tried to let her down gently, but she's finding it all very hard to accept.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: This is a new situation for us, too...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It's such a pity... It seems like the author was only trying to make the story interesting, and the Maison Gardiennage only had Fontaine's best interest in mind...

response.speaker: Charlotte
response.text: Wait... Miss Lepine-Pauline, what are you doing?

response.speaker: Lepine-Pauline
response.text: I'm gonna pick a fight with a Gardemek, head to the Opera Epiclese, and get a one-way ticket to the Fortress of Meropide.

response.speaker: Lepine-Pauline
response.text: That way, I won't have to repay my debts... It's the only way I can afford to keep on living...

response.speaker: Charlotte
response.text: Whoa, there's no need to go that far! I mean... Come on, look at you. You wouldn't even dent the Gardemek's armor — in all likelihood, they'd only hold you up at the Maison Gardiennage for a few days before letting you out. And then you'd still have to repay your debts!

response.speaker: Charlotte
response.text: ...Actually, instead of going into the technicalities of that... How much did you actually invest? How bad can it really be...?

response.speaker: Lepine-Pauline
response.text: ...T—Two hundred and seventy thousand Mora.

response.speaker: Charlotte
response.text: Okay, well... escaping to the Fortress of Meropide over a sum like that seems like a last resort. Surely there must be other options?

response.speaker: Lepine-Pauline
response.text: Not any more... I used to be an equipment supplier to the Fontaine Research Institute before that blew to pieces, and now I'm just a small-time engineer. I scraped together some savings over the past few years, but I put every last Mora into this project, and now I'm left with nothing!

response.speaker: Lepine-Pauline
response.text: It's not just my savings that are gone. It's my whole future as a Graph Adversarial Technology specialist and my dreams of becoming a billionaire one day!

response.speaker: Lepine-Pauline
response.text: Hah... Haha... Heh... *sobs*

response.speaker: Lepine-Pauline
response.text: My life is over.

response.speaker: Charlotte
response.text: Don't despair, Miss Lepine-Pauline. I think I know a way for you to turn this around.

response.speaker: Charlotte
response.text: This prototype you've given me... the "Kamera Lens for Image Recognition Sample Collection" — it's really quite something. You said you designed it specifically for high-fidelity image capture and analysis, yes?

response.speaker: Charlotte
response.text: The rapid focal length adjustment is a very useful function in its own right. It's sure to make many journalists' jobs much easier... In fact, I'd say it has the potential to revolutionize Fontaine's news media!

response.speaker: Charlotte
response.text: So your research efforts thus far are by no means in vain. The technology you've developed may have many applications that you've never even considered.

response.speaker: Lepine-Pauline
response.text: R—Really?

response.speaker: Charlotte
response.text: Absolutely! I've been working as a journalist for The Steambird for a long time now. No one understands the issues we journalists face on a day-to-day basis better than me!

response.speaker: Charlotte
response.text: So keep calm, take heart, and start thinking about mass production. In the meantime, I'll show your invention to all of my colleagues to drum up interest in your product.

response.speaker: Lepine-Pauline
response.text: I can't believe it...

response.speaker: Lepine-Pauline
response.text: If this is true, then... I can look into setting up a whole Kamera lens development pipeline! My big-ticket orders and billionaire aspirations are still on the cards!

response.speaker: Lepine-Pauline
response.text: Maybe I should consider taking out another loan? That way, I can rapidly improve the lens production process, be the first to market, and prepare to battle for dominance in the Kamera industry!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Come on! Stop daydreaming about your pipelines for a minute... Just take it one step at a time and see how it goes. There's no sense putting all your eggs in one basket before things are even off the ground.

choices.text: Being overly ambitious might come back to bite you.

response.speaker: Lepine-Pauline
response.text: Mm-hmm, mm-hmm... And I can probably speak to some people I know and license my image recognition device to a workshop to raise some funds... Ah, I can't believe I didn't think of this sooner!

response.speaker: Lepine-Pauline
response.text: There's no time to lose — I need to get to work! Early bird gets the worm!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ugh, can you believe her? She just ran off!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon's pretty sure our advice went in one ear and out the other.

response.speaker: Charlotte
response.text: It's understandable... When inspiration and passion strike at the same time, it's all too easy to throw yourself headfirst into your work and forget about everyone around you. A lot of journalists are the same way when they're first starting out.

response.speaker: Charlotte
response.text: But don't you worry. I'm gonna write an article on all this, and I'll be checking in on her regularly.

response.speaker: Charlotte
response.text: Her research has the potential to benefit the entire journalistic community. I'll give her plenty of input to stop her from going down any rabbit holes, and make sure mass production of her lens can begin as soon as possible.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It's reassuring to know that you'll be looking out for her, Charlotte!

response.speaker: Charlotte
response.text: Actually... You know what, why don't you two take this prototype lens? I'm sure you'll have plenty of chances to use it on your travels!

response.speaker: Charlotte
response.text: It takes the right person to get the most out of a new technology. In your hands, it's sure to capture some amazing sights.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Thanks a lot, Charlotte!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: No bonus, no biggie! This makes everything worth it.

response.speaker: Charlotte
response.text: You're welcome. I got something out of this too — the beginnings of a very interesting news story!

response.speaker: Charlotte
response.text: The boundaries between real news reports and news-like fiction must not be blurred, even when there's a compelling justification for doing so.

response.speaker: Charlotte
response.text: Yes, that's how I'll phrase it to the editors when I give them my feedback! Let's hope we won't mislead any more well-meaning citizens in the future!

choices.text: Slow and steady wins the race.
She is just a victim of a misunderstanding.
